concept.name: Brier score
concept.definition: The mean squared error of probabilistic forecasts for binary outcomes, and more generally the summed squared probability error across classes under a stated convention.
concept.intuition: It summarizes one aspect of prediction error or decision quality in a number or curve.
concept.mechanics: Subtract each binary outcome from its forecast probability, square the error, and average over held-out cases.
concept.failure_modes: Class imbalance, threshold choice, unequal error costs, outliers, and dependence can make the summary inappropriate or unstable.
concept.misconceptions: No single metric captures economic utility, turnover, risk, calibration, and trading costs at once.
concept.example: Forecasts 0.8 and 0.3 for outcomes 1 and 0 give Brier = (0.04 + 0.09)/2 = 0.065.
